title: Sable: a Performant, Efficient and Scalable Sequence Model for MARL
evidence_location: Section 4; Appendix B.1–B.7; Appendix C Tables 2–6; Appendix D
benchmark_note: 45 main tasks in six suites; NEOM and modified LBF are additional scaling experiments. Do not present the main Sable actor as a local-observation-only decentralized actor.
protocol_note: Main protocol: 10 independent trials per task, 20M environment timesteps per run, 122 evaluation intervals, 32 episodes per interval. Task means and suite IQM use 95% bootstrap intervals. Main baselines: MAT, MAPPO, IPPO, MASAC, HASAC, QMIX; eligibility varies by action space.

title: The Entropy Mechanism of Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Language Models
benchmark_note: Reasoning-language-model RL; retained as conceptual background. It is not a MARL environment benchmark and is excluded from environment-coverage counts.
protocol_note: Its benchmarks and training budgets are outside the MARL environment scope of this edition.

title: Causality-Aware Efficient Exploration for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
evidence_location: Experimental Setup, PDF p.5; Table 1 and Figures 3–5, pp.6–7
benchmark_note: 21 tasks: 4 SMAC, 15 SMACv2 and 2 Google Research Football tasks. Field-of-view restrictions create distinct SMACv2 evaluation settings.
protocol_note: Task counts transcribed; full per-task budgets and seed identifiers are not transcribed in this edition.

title: R3DM: Enabling Role Discovery and Diversity Through Dynamics Models in Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
benchmark_note: SMAC and SMACv2; records SC2 4.10 in the experimental setup. Keep unit compositions and game version with win-rate comparisons.
protocol_note: Uses win rate and cumulative return; the full training budget and evaluation schedule remain to be transcribed.

title: Lazy Agents: A New Perspective on Solving Sparse Reward Problem in Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
benchmark_note: LAIES uses sparse-reward versions of SMAC and Google Research Football. A QMIX dense-reward curve is a distinct reward-setting comparison.
protocol_note: Six random seeds are reported. Reward modifications must be preserved when reproducing the experiment.

title: Learning group collaboration for efficient multi-agent reinforcement learning
evidence_location: Experiments and Testing Environment, PDF pp.5–6
benchmark_note: StarCraft II / SMAC and Google Research Football. Grouping changes the policy communication topology; it does not define a new simulator family.
protocol_note: Per-task training budgets and exact code release are not transcribed or verified in this edition.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Communication-Constrained Priors
benchmark_note: MPE tasks with Markov-based and distance-based communication constraints. Message loss, corruption and the communication graph are experimental variables.
protocol_note: Do not treat these modified communication tasks as the same experiment as unmodified simple_spread. Full task/config transcription is pending.

title: In-Context Fully Decentralized Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
evidence_location: Experiments, PDF p.7 onward; Appendix C
benchmark_note: RAC evaluates matrix games, Predator and Prey, and SMAC. The Predator and Prey implementation is left unresolved here rather than silently equating it to MPE simple_tag.
protocol_note: Reports median performance and standard error over five random seeds. Predator and Prey remains a paper-specific task entry in the paper card.

title: Multi-Agent Guided Policy Optimization
evidence_location: Section 5, PDF pp.6–8; Appendix B; Appendix C
benchmark_note: 43 JAX tasks: CoordSum 4, LBF 7, Connector 4, MPE 3, RWARE 15, SMAX 10. CoordSum replaces MaBrax relative to Sable and SMAX counts differ.
protocol_note: Centralized guidance and decentralized deployment must be recorded separately. This mapping does not import Sable hyperparameters into MAGPO.

title: CAMAR: Continuous Actions Multi-Agent Routing
evidence_location: Experimental Evaluation and Evaluation Protocols, PDF pp.5–7
benchmark_note: Continuous routing benchmark; VMAS is also used for a simulator scalability comparison. Simulator throughput and trained policy quality are separate measurements.
protocol_note: Includes IPPO, MAPPO, IDDPG, MADDPG, ISAC and MASAC plus planning baselines. Record success, path quality and collisions; throughput depends on workload and hardware.

title: Aggregate in the Advantage, Not the Ratio: A Canonical-Form Analysis of Cooperative Multi-Agent Policy Optimization
benchmark_note: Controlled graph-coupled games plus SUMO-RL traffic signals. Appendix C.3 uses a 28×7 grid with 196 signals; it is not a standard SMAC benchmark.
protocol_note: Known coupling graphs and per-agent rewards are essential to this study. Preserve graph, reward support and ratio support separately.

title: Challenges in Credit Assignment for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in Open Agent Systems
source_version: year/venue not independently established; supplied manuscript
benchmark_note: Wildfire WS1 compares closed, agent-open and task-open settings. PistonBall is mentioned as preliminary model validation, not the principal openness benchmark.
protocol_note: 250 evaluation runs with a fixed seed of 42 are reported; that is not evidence of 250 independent training seeds.

title: Scalable Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Agent System
benchmark_note: SS-MARL modifies MPE for safety-aware cooperative navigation. Each agent has its own goal and costs are tracked separately from rewards.
protocol_note: The paper uses 100-step episodes in the discussed safety experiment. Safety costs, thresholds, obstacle counts and population-size transfer must accompany reported return.

title: Controlling Behavioral Diversity in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
benchmark_note: VMAS tasks include multi-agent navigation and cooperative/competitive diversity studies. Parameter sharing and desired System Neural Diversity are experimental factors.
protocol_note: BenchMARL and TorchRL are the reported training stack. Diversity is measured behaviorally; policy entropy alone is not the diversity metric.

title: Mitigating Relative Over-Generalization in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
benchmark_note: Differential games, six modified MPE scenarios and MA-MuJoCo Half-Cheetah. RO-specific reward shaping changes the benchmark relative to default MPE.
protocol_note: Distinguish joint-entry reward/solo-entry penalties, heterogeneous agents/targets, sequential tasks and the trained prey. Full budgets remain to be transcribed.

title: Optimistic Multi-Agent Policy Gradient
benchmark_note: Repeated matrix games, Multi-Agent MuJoCo and Overcooked. Task-specific penalties in the didactic games probe relative overgeneralization.
protocol_note: Do not replace MA-MuJoCo with MaBrax and retain the same reference scores. Preserve Overcooked layouts and sparse/shaped reward settings.
